recipes.name: Eric's Best New York Style Cheesecake

steps.text: Bring all ingredients to room temperature. Place oven shelf in the center of oven and preheat to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Wrap the outside of a 9 inch springform pan with foil. Generously butter the inside of the pan.

In a large bowl, beat cream cheese and butter until smooth. Mix in sugar and cornstarch. Blend in sour cream and whipping cream. Add amaretto and vanilla. Stir in eggs and egg yolk one at a time, mixing thoroughly between each addition. Pour batter into prepared pan.

Pour mixture into prepared springform pan. Place pan in another pan at least one inch wider than cake pan and add warm water to the outer pan to create a water bath for the cake (this prevents cracks in your cheesecake). Bake on the center rack of oven for 70 minutes.
Turn oven off and allow to cool with oven door open for one hour. Then remove cake from water bath and chill at least 3 hours before removing from springform pan.

raw_recipe.headline: Eric's Best New York Style Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This rich crustless cheesecake is flavored with amaretto rather than the traditional lemon. Serve with fresh sliced fruit or berries and fresh whipped cream.

review.reviewBody: I'm rating this the best even though I had some problems. It has a wonderful flavor. I didn't use the amaretto, just vanilla. But mine wouldn't get done. It was way too jiggly at the set time. It also puffed out over the sides of the pan so I think next time I'll try a 10 inch pan. When it cooled the edges tore off, but I made it look alright by adding a whipped cream edge and strawberry sauce on top. I will definitely use this recipe again and try to make it turn out right the next time!

I've made this twice now, and without a doubt, this is the BEST cheesecake we've ever had! I did use fresh squeezed lemon juice instead of alcohol, and followed another reviewers advise in regards to temp. Turned it down to 325 after 20 minutes and baked it for 70mins. Came out perfectly, and it is just so delicious! The first time I made it in a 9' spring form, but halved the recipe. Made plenty of batter still. Second time I used a 10' spring form, again turning down the temp after 20 mins so the cake wouldn't get too brown on top. I had to bake it quite a bit longer that way though, probably closer to 1.5 hours. Well worth it. My husband probably ate 1/2 the cake by himself within the first 2 days Awesome recipe!

I turned this cheesecake into a white chocolate raspberry cheesecake. I did not use the lemon. I did use vanilla and added 8 oz. of Baker's white chocolate, melted and cooled. I poured half of batter into pan. Then I opened up a can of Solo Raspberry filling and dolloped a few spoonfuls on it, then added the rest of the batter and dolloped the rest of the raspberry filling on top. Then I took a butter knife and swirl the raspberry. I cooked the cheesecake for the time given in the recipe. This turned out absolutely FANTASTIC! I will NO longer be buying from the Cheesecake Factory. This was way BETTER according to our dinner guests. BEST cheesecake I have had since 1981. I will be making this again. I almost forgot to mention that I added the eggs last. I didn't want to over mix the eggs. Adding the eggs in the middle of the recipe worried me, so I added the eggs last, and I added them one at a time.

I made this Cheesecake and I doubled the recipe because I needed more than one. The recipe does make more batter than would fit into a 9 inch spring form pan. By doubling the ingredient I got 1- 10 in , 1- 9 in, and 1- 8in cheesecake and still had batter left that I could have made another 8 in had I had another pan.

I read many of the reviews to see what others had done, I did not see where anyone stated how much they were filling the pans, I filled mine 1/2 full and did NOT experience any overflow.

I also did not cook mine in a hot bath but did as one poster suggester and put a cookie pan on the bottom rack and filled it with water, I baked mine at 300 for 2 hours that seemed to be the most used temp in reading the posts, my cakes did not have cracks in them. I did wrap the pans in foil but I've never done that before and am unsure what its purpose was.

They turned out beautiful and taste delicious. I also did not add the liquor to mine but added more vanilla (2 TBS- Dbl batter recipe)

So this is a great recipe hope my comments help whoever makes it next.

This was a very yummy not to heavy but not to light cheesecake. I did make a couple of changes (I know I hate when I read that in a reiview but keep reading) I split the batter into 2 nine inch bunt pans since so many people said that they had problems with it over flowing. I did use the water bath method and cooked it at 325 for 90 min as some of the other reviewers recommended. Lastly I swirled a 1/2 cup of sour cream on top before popping it in the oven trying to recreate a childhood memory. I loved it and had quite a few people ask for the recipe! Oh and I used homemade vanilla instead of the Armaretto like many of the reivews said as well.

You can totally steam a cheesecake! I mixed up Eric's Best and placed it in the oven to find it cold. The oven is broken, it's 9:30 on Christmas eve, I have a pot of soupy sweet cheese and no way to bake it. 

I pulled out my big stock pot. The spring form fits inside. I placed the cake on a steaming rack to keep it off the bottom and added an inch of water. A 9" pan lid fit well on the spring form as a rain hat. The cake steamed for a little over 2 hours. (We watched Jurassic World as it perked) I was nervous slicing it after a big dinner with 20 people watching. Silky and consistent all the way through, it was a big hit.

my oven must be fast, didn't take full 70 minutes. also i substituted Chambord for the amaretto and layered raspberry filling, pouring 1/2 the batter in pan and marbling more filling on the top. looks great

I've made a variation of this recipe many times. I myself add a tsp of cream of Tartar and also a bit of lemon zest. I also sometimes add a Graham cracker crust as well. I use a bit more almaretto. But my peaves with this recipe are the fact that you do indeed need a larger pan than stated. Even a 10 inch is a bit small. And I found that you need to almost double the cooking time and let cool on a closed oven for about 3 hrs.

Problem solved! On my second attempt of making this delicious recipe, I increased the height of the springform pan by wrapping heavy duty aluminum foil around it. To make the foil extra stiff, I folded it in half before placing it around the pan, whose height I increased by about four (4) inches. Just as I had done with the pan, I buttered the interior of the foil. I also don't place my 10-inch pan into a water bath - don't have another pan large enough to accommodate it. Instead, I place a pan with water on the bottom shelf.

With the newly heightened pan, I was able to prevent the batter from overflowing while it baked. It settled once it came out of the oven and was decidedly decadent when I served it. Yummy enough to stand on its own without any garnish or sauces, but that's not a requirement. Here's to eating cake!

Creamy excellence! Added a crust because we prefer that, and used vanilla and lemon juice instead of amaretto. Otherwise followed filling recipe exactly as written. 375 was too hot, the top got a bit brown, will try 325 next time and just bake longer. Did use water bath. So so good! Will definitely make again.
I used a round layer cake pan and reduced the temperature so that it did not overflow the pan. (This tip was detailed in another comment.)Turned out perfectly!
Taste is fantastic, I used lemon juice and jest instead of liquor. Definitely a keeper. I added no strawberries or cherries for topping, this cheesecake stands alone just in flavor. Amazing.

I Having grown up in a house where my mom made the best cheesecakes, I have to give this a failing grade. There is no crust so it cannot be placed on serving platter. First the 375° is too hot! Thus the dark edges and only baked 40 minutes. And I baked it at 350°. Cheesecakes should be baked at 300-325°. The cheesecake shouldn’t brown.
The absolute best cheesecake ever. If you follow the directions to a T, you can’t mess it up. You’ll be asked to make this all the time. Honestly the best I’ve ever had.
Slight addition. ½ oz of Chambord. Turned out amazing.
I've made about (20) of these, all were a hit but one. I dropped that one.
It was really easy to make and hicka good thank you Eric
disaster. Do not waste your time and $

No changes, excellent decadent cheese cake. A family favorite, the only cheesecake l only make. Best if set in refrigerator overnight, I usually make a cream topping by mixing together sour cream, a little sugar and vanilla extract. So good !
Best recipe i tried
